subject: TrueCap #20 — mortgage points: when paying for the rate makes sense
preheader: $8k buy-down vs $8k invested · The 4-year break-even rule · Why most points buyers regret it

marketSnapshot.headline: Q4 cycle update: rates settled, time to price-shop lenders
marketSnapshot.body: 30Y fixed at 6.04%, lowest read in 18 months. The rate-cut narrative has played out — futures price flat-to-mild-cuts through 2027. Lenders are now competing on origination volume rather than waiting for the next leg lower. The practical result: lender quotes vary more this month than they have in a year. On a $300k rental loan, I've seen quote-to-quote spreads of 30-45bp from the SAME borrower applying to 3 different lenders in the same week. Take the time to get 3+ quotes on any deal you're closing. The pricing variance is real money.

dealSpotter.body: $285k 3/2. Lender quote: 6.04% with no points, OR 5.29% with 2.5 points ($7,125). Monthly P&I difference: $182. Break-even on the $7,125 cost: 39 months (3.25 years). If you'll hold longer than 4 years, points win. If you're planning to refi when rates drop another 50bp+ (possible in 2027 if cuts continue), points lose because you give up the buy-down on refi. The right answer depends on your exit timeline AND your view on rates.

dealSpotter.address: Kansas City, MO — Volker neighborhood SFR
dealSpotter.headlineNumber: Skip points · take the rate · keep capital
dealSpotter.body: $225k 3/2. Lender offers same buy-down: $6,500 for 75bp off rate. For this investor profile — likely to refi if rates drop another 30-50bp, building portfolio, capital constrained — taking the higher rate and keeping the $6,500 deployed elsewhere is the better move. The $6,500 invested as down payment on another property generates more cash flow than the $115/mo of P&I savings.

$165k 3/2. Investor plans to hold this 10-15 years as the neighborhood gentrifies. Lender quote: 5.79% with 1.5 points ($2,475). Break-even: 28 months. Holding period: 10+ years. The locked-in rate also acts as a hedge — if Frankford's economy outpaces inflation and rents grow strongly, the fixed 5.79% gets cheaper in real terms every year. Long-hold + appreciation = points are insurance worth paying for.

blogFeature.title: How to underwrite a rental property in 60 seconds
blogFeature.excerpt: The five numbers that decide whether a rental deal pencils. Once you know the framework, the buy-points-or-not decision becomes obvious — it's whether the points improve or worsen those five numbers over your holding period.

qa.question: Simple rule for when to buy mortgage points and when to skip them?
qa.answer: Three-factor decision. (1) Hold period: if you'll own the property longer than the break-even (typically 30-48 months), points win. If you'll sell or refi sooner, points lose. (2) Rate outlook: if you believe rates will be 50bp+ lower in the next 2-3 years AND you'd refi at that point, skip points (the refi cancels the buy-down). If you believe rates will be flat-to-higher, lock in the buy-down. (3) Capital allocation: every dollar in points is a dollar not in another investment. If you have $30k available and the choice is 'buy 3 points on this deal' or 'use it as down payment on a second property,' the second property almost always wins because it produces both cash flow AND principal pay-down AND appreciation, while points only reduce one line item. Default rule: buy points only when you'll hold 4+ years AND you've already deployed the capital you have available elsewhere. The most common mistake is buying points to make a marginal deal pencil — the deal that only works with paid-down rates is a fragile deal.
